groups.title: Sauce Base
items: Fresh cilantro stalks (for sauce) and tops (for garnish)

steps: Prepare the Chicken: Cut chicken into smaller, bite-sized pieces for quicker cooking.

Marinate the Chicken: In a bowl, combine the chicken with salt, pepper, turmeric, cumin, coriander, cayenne, garam masala, yogurt, and oil. Mix well and let it sit. For best results, marinate overnight.

Start the Sauce Base: Heat a pan until smoking. Add grapeseed oil and sliced red onions. Caramelize the onions. Bash cardamom seeds to release fragrance and add to the pan. Add sliced ginger, chili (with seeds), and garlic. Continue cooking until onions break down.
Add Butter and Cilantro Stalks to Sauce: Add butter to the onions, ginger, garlic, and chili mixture. Incorporate cilantro stalks.
Toast Spices in Sauce: Lightly dust the sauce base with garam masala, turmeric, cumin, and cayenne, toasting them in the butter.
Cook the Chicken: In a separate hot pan, add the marinated chicken and cook to get some color on all sides.
Combine Sauce Components: Add tomato sauce and double cream to the caramelized onion mixture. Bring to a boil.
Season the Sauce: Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and lemon juice to brighten the flavors.
Blend the Sauce: Transfer the sauce mixture to a blender and blend until it becomes a smooth, velvety consistency.
Strain the Sauce (Optional but Recommended): Pass the blended sauce through a sieve to remove any whole spices or fibrous bits, creating an even smoother sauce.
Combine Chicken and Sauce: Add the cooked chicken to the strained sauce. Scrape any remaining flavor from the chicken pan into the sauce.

Finish the Dish: Add a couple of knobs of butter and lemon zest to the chicken and sauce. Stir gently on low heat without boiling. Correct final seasoning with salt and pepper. Stir in fresh cilantro just before serving.
Serve: Serve hot with rice or homemade chapatis.
notes: Note: I used the pre mix powder so no need to prep powder separately
